summary: Second runner invocation for step M1-S03 of build tier2-webhook, after the operator amended the step under remedy B and re-claimed it as running. The owning agent apex-builder was executed inline per AGENT.md Step 6's any-other-host clause and returned a package this time rather than a refusal: 25 files under artefacts/M1-S03/, of which all 20 declared outputs are present and 5 are undeclared. check-outputs exited 0 with no missing, empty or malformed paths, all three declared checkers exited 0 with zero findings at any severity, and both envelopes validate, so the step was set built. Nothing was written outside artefacts/M1-S03/ and envelopes/M1-S03/, nothing was deployed, no test was run against an org, no gate was written, and M1-S04's artefacts were not touched. The run carries one P1 the human should read before the milestone gate: remedy B removed the trigger kill switch along with the template that provided it.
confidence_rationale: MEDIUM per this agent's Step 9 table: five undeclared artefacts appeared under artefacts/M1-S03/, which is the table's MEDIUM row. Everything else is the HIGH row - the step was legitimately claimed, every required input of the owning agent resolved from plan.json alone, check-outputs exited 0, both envelopes validate, and no file landed outside the step's artefact directory. The undeclared five are a plan gap rather than an owning-agent defect: the step's templates[] cites two template classes its outputs[] does not declare, and apex-builder's provenance rule requires them shipped.

process_observations.observation: The blocked-amend-rebuild cycle worked exactly as standards/build-orchestration.md section 2 describes: the refusal named two specific remedies, a human chose one, amend-step recorded the prior inputs[] and templates[] in full, and the rebuild read the amended record rather than the message that announced it - so the second run is reproducible from plan.json alone.

Every declared acceptance test that a runner can execute passed on the first attempt of the rebuilt package, with zero findings at any severity rather than zero blocking findings, so the step reaches the tester with nothing already accepted as a standing warning.

process_observations.observation: The step declares 20 outputs and its owning agent legitimately produced 25 files, because the step's templates[] cites two template classes whose copies apex-builder's provenance rule requires it to ship and whose paths outputs[] never declared - the same mismatch M1-S04's run 1 recorded, now on its second step.

The step's acceptance-test description for the callouts checker states the opposite of what that checker's code does - it says the checker fails on a test with setMock after startTest, while the code flags a setMock with no preceding startTest - so a reader debugging a failure from PLAN.md would be sent the wrong way.

Remedy B bought a deployable build by dropping three canonical templates, and the owning agent recorded the loss as a P1 rather than absorbing it - the org now has no trigger kill switch and no data-load bypass, which is a decision a human made on the plan and a human should re-read at the milestone gate rather than discover during a load.

The runner's Wave 10 persistence names docs/reports/build-step-runner/<run_id>.{md,json} alongside the build-scoped pair, while the invocation constrained writes to the build directory; the build-scoped pair was written and the docs/reports/ pair was not.
The step is built and its declared tests have not been run by the agent that owns running them.

section_3_1_support_gaps: Neither build_plan.py validate nor the plan verifier's grounding lens reads the body of a cited template, so a templates[] entry needing a second template or a custom metadata type passes plan time and fails at the builder. It cost this build two refusals across its two Apex steps. A plan-time check that greps each cited templates/apex/** file for other template class names and for __c / __mdt tokens, warning when the closure is not covered by some step's outputs[], would have caught both at plan time.

A step's outputs[] cannot be corrected once the step leaves pending, so the template copies apex-builder's provenance rule obliges it to ship stay permanently undeclared and permanently unverified by check-outputs. Every Apex step in this build has the same five-file gap. Either the planner declares template copies up front, or section 4's Apex-foundations step owns them in one place - the feature tier's five-step ceiling is what discourages the latter, and it carves out only the manifest step.

The runner's Wave 10 persistence names a docs/reports/build-step-runner/ pair alongside the build-scoped envelope, while section 2's layout puts agent envelopes under envelopes/<step-id>/. The invocation constrained writes to the build directory, so only the build-scoped pair was written; the contract does not say which wins.
